dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a measure μ, real-valued function X, and real exponent p, this is defined to be the extended nonnegative integral ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal ((|X(ω)|).rpow p) ∂μ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The left side of the second conjunct unfolds to exactly its right side, so that conjunct is a definitional self-equality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a measure μ and real-valued function X, this is defined to be the real-valued Bochner integral ∫ ω, X(ω) ∂μ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the integral used both in LocalDef003 and explicitly on the right side of the first conjunct.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For μ, X, and n : Nat, this is defined as LocalDef002 μ applied to the pointwise natural power ω ↦ X(ω)^n, hence as the real integral of X^n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Unfolding this definition makes the first conjunct exactly an equality of LocalDef002 μ (ω ↦ X(ω)^n) with itself.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: The logical conjunction of two propositions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It requires both displayed definitional equalities simultaneously.

dependency_coverage.name: ENNReal
dependency_coverage.meaning: The extended nonnegative real type, implemented as nonnegative reals with an added top element.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the codomain of LocalDef001, ENNReal.ofReal, and the extended nonnegative integral in the second conjunct, so no finiteness is asserted.

dependency_coverage.name: ENNReal.ofReal
dependency_coverage.meaning: It sends a real r to an extended nonnegative real through r.toNNReal, thereby discarding any negative part before embedding it in ENNReal.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It converts the real value (|X(ω)|).rpow p into the ENNReal-valued integrand of the second conjunct.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq

binders: An arbitrary type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
An arbitrary measure μ on Ω.
An arbitrary function X : Ω → ℝ.
hypotheses: The real exponent p is strictly positive: 0 < p.
conclusions: LocalDef003(μ, X, n) equals LocalDef002(μ, ω ↦ X(ω)^n); after unfolding LocalDef003, this is the self-equality of the real integral of the pointwise natural power X^n.
LocalDef001(μ, X, p) equals ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal ((|X(ω)|).rpow p) ∂μ; after unfolding LocalDef001, this is the self-equality of that extended nonnegative integral.
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef002(μ, Y) := ∫ ω, Y(ω) ∂μ, a Real-valued Bochner integral.
LocalDef003(μ, X, n) := LocalDef002(μ, ω ↦ X(ω)^n) = ∫ ω, X(ω)^n ∂μ.
LocalDef001(μ, X, p) := ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal ((|X(ω)|).rpow p) ∂μ.
The power X(ω)^n is the natural-number power from the real multiplicative monoid, whereas (|X(ω)|).rpow p is real exponentiation with real exponent p.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable space Ω, every measure μ on it, every real-valued function X, every natural number n, and every positive real p, two definitional identities hold simultaneously: the quantity defined as the integral of X raised pointwise to n equals that same integral, and the quantity defined as the extended nonnegative integral of the p-th real power of |X| equals that same extended nonnegative integral. Thus both conjuncts merely unfold the supplied local definitions.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The only explicit assumption is 0 < p; it is not used to establish either equality, so the displayed conjunction is definitionally true even without substantive use of positivity.
There is no measurability or integrability hypothesis on X or its powers.
There is no assumption that μ is a probability measure, a finite measure, or even a nonzero measure.
The natural exponent n is unrestricted and may be 0.
The first value lies in Real through a totalized integral operation, so without integrability assumptions it need not express a classical finite raw moment in the usual analytic sense.
The second value lies in ENNReal and is not asserted to be finite; ENNReal.ofReal also clips negative real inputs, although its input here is a real power of an absolute value.

Because each right side exactly repeats the corresponding definition on the left, the proposition makes no nontrivial claim about moments, existence, finiteness, or relationships between the natural and real exponents.
ambiguities: The one-level bodies of MeasureTheory.integral and MeasureTheory.lintegral are opaque wrapper projections in the packet, so their exact conventions for nonintegrable or nonmeasurable functions cannot be recovered here; the target's two definitional self-equalities do not depend on those conventions.
